column1: *** GENDATABASE.COM - TRIED FOR THE FIRST TIME, 15 September 2026, on David's suggestion. ***
column2: *** gendatabase.com - 'South African Genealogy Search Engine'. Surname 'Lerena' returns 38 results across three indexes: Verified Death Database (15), National Archives (14), Estate File Database (9). ***
column4: *** THIS SOURCE HAD NEVER BEEN TOUCHED. *** The archive's only South African index was NAAIRS, which returns file references and nothing else. *** Gendatabase returns BIRTH YEAR, DEATH YEAR, MARRIAGE YEAR, MAIDEN NAME and SPOUSE *** on its death and estate rows, which is a different order of information. *** The summary rows are free; the full record sits behind a paid account, which this session did not create and did not pay for. ***

column2: *** Surname 'Llerena' - 0 results (0 verified, 0 transcribed). *** The search was confirmed to have actually run: the first attempt returned the cached 'Lerena' page with an identical timing figure and was discarded rather than recorded.
column4: *** A REAL NULL, AND IT SUPPORTS THE SPELLING STORY. *** This archive argues that Andalusian *** Llerena *** was smoothed to *** Lerena *** by River Plate clerks within a generation. *** The South African branch carries only the reduced form - not one Llerena in a billion-record index. *** Sancho's own marriage act of 1791 still writes Llerena. The change had finished before the family reached the Cape.

column1: *** THE THREE SONS OF THE 1950 ESTATE NOW HAVE DEATH DATES ***
column2: The estate of *** Robert Paul Lerena of Newlands, died 19 March 1950 *** named three major sons: LOUIS, NUNO FERNANDO and RICHARDO JUAN CARLOS. Gendatabase carries an estate file for each: *** 'LERENA, NUNO FERNANDO' - ZA TAB MHG 6746/71 ***; *** 'LERENA, ROGUE LUIS ARMANDO' - ZA TAB MHG 1518/73 ***; and *** RICARDO JUAN CARLOS LERENA, born 1920, died 1994, married 1941 to Doreen May Chappell ***.
column4: *** THIS IS THE REAL GAIN. *** The archive knew the three sons only as names in their father's liquidation account. It now has *** an approximate death year for each *** and a file reference to order. *** ONE INFERENCE, FLAGGED AS AN INFERENCE: *** the estate's 'LOUIS LERENA' is very likely the 'ROGUE LUIS ARMANDO LERENA' of MHG 1518/73 - Roque Luis Armando, using his middle name - but *** nobody has opened either file and the identification is NOT established. ***

column2: *** Born 1920, died 1994; married 1941 to DOREEN MAY CHAPPELL, born 1921, died 1999. ***
column4: *** HE CARRIES HIS GRANDFATHER'S NAME. *** Pablo Armando's 1908 enrolment card names his own father as *** JUAN CARLOS LERENA ***. Here is a grandson christened Ricardo *** Juan Carlos ***. *** The naming runs true across three generations and two continents ***, which is the kind of thing that argues for the Argentine and South African families being one family. *** And CHAPPELL returns: *** this archive already had to correct a claim that Roque's first wife was a Chappell. *** On this index the Chappell married RICARDO JUAN CARLOS, not Roque. *** The correction stands and is now better explained.

column1: *** THE NEXT GENERATION, AS THE INDEX HAS IT ***
column2: *** ROBERTO JUAN ROQUE LERENA, b.1944 d.2022 ***, married 1969 to BRIGITTE ZAAGE (b.1951 d.2023). *** ANTON ARMANDO LERENA, b.1952 d.2003 ***, divorced 2001 - matching NAAIRS TPD 1367/1980, 'Glynnis Margaret Lerena (born Bolton) versus Anton Armando Lerena'. Also Catherine Tertia Karon (nee Lerena, b.1952), Patricia Carmen MacEwan (nee Lerena, b.1958), Jeanette Marie Riekstins (nee Lerena, b.1949 d.2021), Paul Raymond Lerena (b.1951 d.2000), Rhena May Lerena (nee Barichievy, b.1913 d.1998).
column4: *** UNPLACED, AND DELIBERATELY LEFT UNPLACED. *** Every one of these is a candidate descendant and not one of them is attached to the line by a document. *** They are recorded as an index harvest, not as a family tree. *** Note also a live contradiction: *** this index says Anton Armando Lerena was born 1952 and died 2003; the archive's existing row from ancestors.co.za says he died in 2013 aged 68, implying birth about 1945. *** Those cannot both be right about one man, and they may simply be two men. *** Not merged. ***

column1: *** A PATTERN THAT NEEDS CHECKING BEFORE IT IS BELIEVED ***
column2: *** Five of the fifteen death rows carry the year 1999: *** Catherine Tertia Karon (b.1952), Gayle Lerena nee Preston (b.1952), Pierre Frederick Lerena (b.1948), *** Jeffrey Lerena (b.1991) *** and *** Richard Lerena (b.1986) *** - including a married couple and two children aged eight and thirteen.
column4: *** EITHER SOMETHING TERRIBLE HAPPENED TO THIS FAMILY IN 1999, OR THE INDEX HAS AN ARTEFACT. *** A default or padded year is common in transcribed death indexes and would produce exactly this cluster. *** This archive will not assert either reading from a summary row. *** It is written down as a question, to be settled by the actual death notices, and it is the first thing to check if a subscription is ever bought.

column1: *** WHAT A PAID ACCOUNT WOULD BUY ***
column2: *** Full record detail - which on a South African death notice means exact dates, place, occupation, marital status, the surviving spouse, and crucially THE NAMES OF THE PARENTS. *** The site advertises birth, marriage, death, baptism and estate records.
column4: *** A DECISION FOR DAVID, NOT FOR THIS SESSION. *** This session does not create accounts and does not pay for things. *** The single highest-value purchase would be the death notice of RICARDO JUAN CARLOS LERENA (d.1994) ***, because a South African death notice names the deceased's parents - which would state, in a modern official document, *** who his father was, and so tie the Cape family to Pablo Armando in writing rather than by inference. ***
